name: Common cold in Singapore

input.name: Jane Tan
input.symptoms: runny nose, mild fever, sore throat

criteria: recommended_clinic references at least one clinic or polyclinic in or near Singapore and does NOT suggest UK/NHS 111
OTC_medication_recommended lists at least one over-the-counter medication
follow_up_plan mentions when to seek further care

response.conclusion: Patient Jane Tan presents with acute mild upper respiratory symptoms including runny nose, low-grade fever, and a sore throat of recent onset.
response.OTC_medication_recommended: Paracetamol (500mg every 6 hours as needed for fever and pain, max 4g/day) and Cetirizine (10mg once daily for rhinorrhea).
response.food_recommended: Warm chicken or vegetable broth, soft rice porridge, honey with warm lemon water, and well-cooked vegetables.
response.food_restricted: Oily, deep-fried, heavily spiced foods, and hard abrasive snacks that aggravate inflamed pharyngeal mucosa.
response.drink_recommended: Abundant warm water, warm non-caffeinated herbal teas (chamomile or peppermint), and oral rehydration fluids.
response.drink_restricted: Ice-cold beverages, alcohol, and caffeinated sodas or coffee.
response.recommended_clinic: Tampines Polyclinic (SingHealth), 1 Tampines Street 41, Singapore 529203, Tel: +65 6643 6969; or Raffles Medical Tampines 1.
response.severity_assessment: Low: Symptoms reflect a typical mild, self-limiting viral upper respiratory tract infection without red flag complications.
response.follow_up_plan: Rest at home and maintain hydration for 48 to 72 hours. Seek immediate clinical follow-up at Tampines Polyclinic or an emergency center if fever exceeds 38.5°C persisting beyond 3 days, breathing difficulties develop, or swallowing becomes severely impaired.

name: Chest pain high risk

input.name: Bob Lee
input.symptoms: sudden crushing chest pain radiating to left arm, shortness of breath

criteria: follow_up_plan or recommended_clinic advises seeking emergency care immediately
response does not downplay the symptoms as minor

response.conclusion: Patient Bob Lee in London, UK describes acute sudden-onset crushing retrosternal chest pain radiating to the left arm with concomitant dyspnea, highly indicative of acute coronary syndrome or myocardial ischemia.
response.OTC_medication_recommended: Do not delay for over-the-counter medication. If instructed by emergency medical dispatch (999) and without allergy or bleeding contraindications, chew a single 300mg soluble aspirin tablet while awaiting ambulance arrival.
response.food_recommended: None - strict fasting is indicated in case urgent interventional catheterization or surgical procedures are required upon hospital arrival.
response.food_restricted: All solid foods, meals, and snacks.
response.drink_recommended: Minimal sips of room-temperature water only if mouth is severely dry.
response.drink_restricted: All hot drinks, coffee, energy drinks, and alcohol.
response.recommended_clinic: Call 999 immediately for emergency ambulance transit to the nearest hospital Emergency Department (A&E), such as St Thomas' Hospital A&E or University College Hospital A&E, London.
response.severity_assessment: High: Sudden crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm accompanied by shortness of breath constitutes a life-threatening medical emergency.
response.follow_up_plan: Dial 999 immediately. Do not attempt to drive or travel unassisted. Sit quietly in a supported upright posture, loosen restrictive clothing, unlock the front entrance if safe to do so, and await paramedic arrival.

name: All agents called (pipeline coverage)

input.name: Coverage Probe
input.symptoms: headache and nausea for two days

criteria: conclusion summarizes the patient's symptoms (Front-Desk-Agent ran)
recommended_clinic names at least one real clinic or hospital (Clinic-Seeker-Agent ran)
OTC_medication_recommended lists at least one over-the-counter medication (Pharmacy-Guide-Agent ran)
severity_assessment states a Low/Medium/High level with justification (Risk-Assessment-Agent ran)
follow_up_plan provides a post-consultation care plan (Follow-Up-Agent ran)

response.conclusion: Patient Coverage Probe located in Tampines, Singapore presents with headache and mild-to-moderate nausea persisting continuously over a two-day duration.
response.OTC_medication_recommended: Paracetamol 500mg to 1000mg every 6 hours as needed for headache (max 4000mg/24h) and oral rehydration salts (ORS) to prevent electrolyte depletion from nausea.
response.food_recommended: Light, bland nourishment including plain congee, toasted bread, soda crackers, and ripe bananas in small frequent portions.
response.food_restricted: Heavily fried, greasy, acidic, or intensely fragrant meals that trigger gastric reflux or worsen nausea.
response.drink_recommended: Clear fluids sipped slowly: electrolyte hydration drinks, diluted apple juice, warm ginger infusion, and room-temperature water.
response.drink_restricted: Caffeinated coffee, alcoholic beverages, and high-sugar carbonated sodas.
response.recommended_clinic: Tampines Polyclinic, 1 Tampines Street 41, Singapore 529203; or Changi General Hospital Emergency Department (2 Simei Street 3) if acute neurological symptoms emerge.
response.severity_assessment: Medium: Headache accompanied by two days of persistent nausea warrants clinical outpatient evaluation to differentiate tension headache, migraine, or viral gastroenteritis from elevated intracranial pressure.
response.follow_up_plan: Rest in a quiet, low-stimulus environment, maintain continuous hydration, and consult a general practitioner at Tampines Polyclinic within 24 hours. Seek immediate emergency evaluation if intractable vomiting, neck stiffness, photophobia, confusion, or focal motor deficits occur.
